correctness.rationale: Multiplicity gives an additive sum over exact prime powers. In a root class (or at all odd primes for p=2), exponent one adds at least one. The reciprocal-prime theorem for a fixed reduced arithmetic progression makes the sum of 1/q−1/q² diverge. For each finite set, the modulus product of q² gives exact independence in density; Chebyshev bounds the upper density of V<K by μ/(μ−K)² for μ>K, then μ tends to infinity. In the odd non-root case the q=p local factor is 1 modulo p, and no exponent-one factor contributes. The bound ν_p(1+⋯+q^{ar})≤log_p(a+1)+ar log_p q and the count ≤x/q^a yield a convergent majorant ∑_q O_{p,r}((1+log q)/q²), valid for every x≥1. Markov precludes density divergence. In the cyclic group of order p−1 the congruence rj≡(p−1)/2 is soluble exactly when ν₂(r)<ν₂(p−1).
residual_risks: Symbolic review; no rate or parameter-uniformity claimed. The reciprocal-prime formulation, not just infinitude in a progression, is the analytic input.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The reported arbitrary-p,r bound does not give an x-uniform mean or a density-one divergence criterion; Zhao's full text was not available for additional comparison.
